name: final-digit-overshadowing
description: Overshadowing by a visible shared final digit gained ~7 nats over the one_sided_magnitude_bound_overlap incumbent (iter_4)
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested 2026-11-02 (iter_4/candidate_0, final_digit_overshadowing_overlap). When at least 2 examples share a final digit, every other family and both bounds get their salience multiplied by `retain`. Posterior retain was about 0.07, so the overshadowing is strong. Plain arviz LOO with 2 chains: +7.4 ± 2.5 nats over the incumbent. 7 of 51 sets (486 trials) have a shared final digit. The idea came from the critique of shared_final_digit_match_rate.
**Why:** it is the first non-split tweak that gained, unlike the ones in [[overlap-model-tweaks]].
**How to apply:** set-dependent salience gating (one visible pattern overshadowing the others) may also work for other conspicuous patterns, such as all multiples of 10.

Update 2026-11-02 (experiment2 iter_0/candidate_3): adding the seed-multiple family from [[seed-multiple-property]] on top of overshadowing gave plain 2-chain arviz LOO -3168.7 vs -3208.6 for the incumbent alone on the experiment2 data (+40 nats). The posterior retain was about 0.008 and the seed salience about 0.14. Submitted as seed_multiple_digit_overshadowing.

name: graded-consensus-properties
description: Letting partially shared properties count (weight = fraction^gamma) gave +3.2 MAP loglik on final_digit_overshadowing_overlap (exp2)
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested 2026-11-02 (experiment2 iter_0/candidate_1, graded_consensus_feature_overlap). Experiment 2 has 5040 rows and 94 sets. The incumbent's MAP loglik is -3197.1; with every property held by k of n examples weighted (k/n)^gamma, it is -3193.8, with gamma about 2.5. The motivation was 13,91: targets ending in 1 (the last example's digit) get about 0.8 yes, other odd targets about 0.3, and the incumbent predicts about 0.6 for all odd targets. The incumbent also over-predicts 84,94,34 / 78,48,88 / 46,76,66 non-digit targets (0.17 predicted, about 0.03 observed), and under-predicts the 7,63 even multiples of 7 (it has no seed family).
**Why:** the gain is modest. A recency effect (the last example's digit) is the critique's lead and is still untested on exp2.
**How to apply:** next, try last-example weighting or a lower floor for overshadowed sets. See [[final-digit-overshadowing]], [[overlap-model-tweaks]].

name: last-example-digit-recency
description: "Ends like the LAST example" lingering property gave +25.6 MAP loglik on final_digit_overshadowing_overlap (experiment2); first-example +7.6, middle 0
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested 2026-11-02 (experiment2 iter_0/candidate_2, last_example_digit_recency_overlap). MAP log-lik on experiment2 data, incumbent final_digit_overshadowing_overlap = -3197.1. I added "ends in the last example's final digit" (only when the examples do not all share a digit) with salience recency*sal[final digit]:
- last example: -3171.5 (+25.6, recency about 0.84); any example: +14.5; first example: +7.6; middle examples only: 0.
- All of the last example's unshared properties at a discount: +4.3; first example's: -3.
**Why:** it is a real order (recency) effect, specific to the final digit. It addresses the critique's last_vs_first_example_digit statistic.
**How to apply:** more order effects may be in digit and surface features rather than arithmetic ones. See [[final-digit-overshadowing]].

name: leaky-memory-recency
description: Leaky memory for earlier examples (recency) on the overshadowing overlap model gave ~0 gain on experiment2 data
metadata:
  type: project
---

name: overlap-model-tweaks
description: Which tweaks to the salience feature-overlap models gained or did nothing (iter_3 tests, 2-chain arviz LOO)
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested 2026-11-02 on top of decimal_multiple_salience_overlap (8 families). Plain arviz LOO was -1477.4 here; the pipeline's grouped ELPD differs.
- Splitting parity into separate odd and even salience: about +6 nats (even 0.11 vs odd 0.04). Submitted as iter_3/candidate_5 parity_direction_salience_overlap.
- ~0 gain (iter_4/candidate_2, on the one_sided incumbent): a shared final digit scaling down arithmetic-family salience ("search termination"); stop param stayed near its prior, LOO -1464.95 vs -1465.19.
- ~0 gain: size-principle property weights, slope or intercept scaled by set size, span salience scaled by set size, each family counted once, a power on overlap, a "no pattern" constant in the denominator, a separate ends-in-0/5 family, position weighting with the decimal family added.
**Why:** this model space is nearly saturated, so new family splits are where gains came from.
**How to apply:** try salience-family splits before reshaping the combination rule. See [[pytensor-gather-speed]].

Iter_4 (2026-11-02), tested on one_sided_magnitude_bound_overlap (plain arviz LOO -1465.2, 2 chains):
- Extra logit boost when the target ends in a final digit shared by 2+ examples: -1462.0 (+3.2; fd_boost about 0.85). This addresses the critique that shared final digits are under-endorsed. Submitted as iter_4/candidate_4 shared_final_digit_rule_overlap.
- Odd/even parity split grafted on: -1461.5 (+3.7). Not submitted.

iter_4 tests (2026-11-02, plain arviz LOO, 2 chains; incumbent one_sided_magnitude_bound_overlap = -1465.2):
- Parity split plus one-sided bounds: -1461.2 (+4). Submitted as iter_4/candidate_5 parity_split_one_sided_bound_overlap.
- Tversky contrast logit (a + b*matched - c*missed) in place of the ratio: -1472.4 (-7). Worse.
- Shared-final-digit critique: the final-digit salience is already ~0.48. The under-endorsement comes from the ~0.69 ceiling for full matches (only the 28,98 set has these targets; its shared multiple of 7 dilutes the overlap). This is still unsolved.

Update 2026-11-02 (iter_4/candidate_3), on top of one_sided_magnitude_bound_overlap (plain arviz LOO -1465.2):
- Gain of about +4.5 nats (-1460.6): make the slope grow with the shared profile's total salience. The slope becomes slope + gain*10*den, which is the same as adding the absolute matched salience to the logit. Submitted as salience_scaled_decisiveness_overlap.
- ~0 gain: Tversky-style distinctive features of the target in the denominator (beta went to 0), a separate family for multiples of 7/11/12 (+4 at MAP but degenerate), and the slope times den^gamma.
- Why it works: every target that fully matches its set had a predicted yes-rate capped near 0.7. In the data, matches to sets that share only parity get about 0.6, and final-digit, 5/10 or power matches get 0.8-1.0.

name: pytensor-gather-speed
description: In these PyMC candidates, gathering a parameter-dependent tensor by integer index is slow; one-hot matmul is ~5x faster
metadata:
  type: project
---
Indexing a large parameter-dependent tensor like post[cell_set] (shape cells×rules×widths) made the gradient 37 ms per eval. Changing it to a one-hot (cells×sets) matrix times post reshaped to (sets, -1), and pooling the widths into 24 log-spaced bands, brought it down to 7 ms. The incumbent rule_within_range_conjunction takes about 3 ms. The check_candidate smoke fit (200 iterations) takes about 4 min at 37 ms and 47 s at 7 ms. Full admission allows 30 min per run.
**Why:** admission rejects slow fits; I found this on 2026-11-01 (iter_1 candidate_3).
**How to apply:** benchmark compile_dlogp before running the check. Compute per distinct set, then send results to cells with a one-hot matmul.

name: seed-multiple-property
description: "Smallest example divides all others → multiples-of-it property" gave +10 MAP loglik on the overlap model; gcd/spacing/coincidence/contrast/specificity tweaks gave ~0
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested 2026-11-02 (iter_4/candidate_1) as MAP log-lik on top of one_sided_magnitude_bound_overlap (incumbent MAP -1454.8):
- Seed-multiple family (min example ≥2 divides all examples; target is a multiple of it), with its own Dirichlet salience: -1444.8 (+10 for 1 param). Submitted as seed_multiple_salience_overlap. It helps 7,63 (even multiples of 7 accepted), 81,9, 8,64.
- ~0: gcd of the examples as seed, residue-mod-m "spacing" family, coincidence weight (1-b^n)^gamma, slope scaled by profile specificity.
- Worse (-1462): Tversky contrast (absolute match minus mismatch) instead of the ratio.
- The incumbent tops out near p=0.71 for full matches; 28,98 targets ending in 8 are seen ~0.9 (the critique's final-digit miss). Nothing tried fixed that.
**How to apply:** relations between the examples (one dividing another) are where new signal is; see [[overlap-model-tweaks]].

Update 2026-11-02 (experiment2 iter_0/candidate_4): grafted the seed family onto final_digit_overshadowing_overlap, with the seed salience also discounted by `retain`. Submitted as seed_multiple_digit_overshadowing_overlap. The smoke check passed and a fit takes about 6 s. Its ELPD was not measured before submitting. The two mechanisms affect different sets, so their gains may add up. See [[final-digit-overshadowing]].

name: seed-plus-digit-overshadowing
description: Seed-multiple model plus final-digit overshadowing gave MAP loglik -3174, vs -3197 for the incumbent and -3262 for the seed model (experiment2 iter_0)
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested 2026-11-02 (experiment2 iter_0/candidate_5, seed_multiple_digit_overshadowing). Full-data MAP log-likelihoods:
- seed model alone: -3262
- final_digit_overshadowing_overlap (incumbent): -3197
- seed model with digit overshadowing grafted on: -3174 (retain about 0.002). Submitted.
- seed model where the seed relation itself overshadows the other properties: -3252. Weak.
The LOO gaps are much smaller than the MAP gaps (incumbent vs seed: 8 nats LOO, 65 at MAP). The digit-overshadowing gain likely rests on a few sets.
**How to apply:** see [[final-digit-overshadowing]] and [[seed-multiple-property]]. The two mechanisms stack.

critique
Refinement of `seed_multiple_salience_overlap`. I kept its account: people say "yes" in proportion to the salience-weighted share of the examples' shared property profile that the target also has, and they treat "multiples of the smallest example" as a salient property when that example divides all the others. The one change is grafted from `final_digit_overshadowing_overlap`: when several examples visibly share a final digit, that pattern overshadows every other shared property (the seed multiple, parity, other multiples, the magnitude bounds, and so on), and those properties all lose an inferred fraction of their salience. As a result, the seed-multiple account predicts strong digit-based generalization on shared-final-digit sets (28, 98 -> 18, 38 endorsed; 14, 56 rejected) while keeping generalization along multiples of the seed for sets like 7, 63.

"""Last-example final-digit recency on the overshadowing overlap model.

Refinement of final_digit_overshadowing_overlap by one order-dependent change:
people revise a running guess while reading the examples in order, and the
final digit of the LAST example shown lingers as a candidate pattern ("ends in
d") even when not all examples share it. "Yes" is still a sigmoid of the
salience-weighted share of the shared property profile the target has (family
saliences, base-ten multiples own family, one-sided magnitude bounds, shared
visible final digit overshadowing the other properties), but the profile also
holds "ends like the last example" with salience = recency * final-digit
salience. Targets sharing the last example's final digit are thus endorsed
more than ones sharing the first example's.
"""
import numpy as np
import pymc as pm

_N = range(1, 101)
N_FAM = 8  # family 5 = final digit; bounds are salience entries 8, 9
FD = 5


def _props():
    props = []
    props.append((0, {n for n in _N if n % 2 == 1}))
    props.append((0, {n for n in _N if n % 2 == 0}))
    props.append((1, {n for n in _N if n > 1 and all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1))}))
    props.append((2, {k * k for k in range(1, 11)}))
    props.append((2, {k ** 3 for k in range(1, 5)}))
    for b in range(2, 11):
        props.append((3, {b ** k for k in range(1, 8) if b ** k <= 100}))
    for m in range(3, 13):
        fam = 7 if m in (5, 10) else 4
        props.append((fam, {n for n in _N if n % m == 0}))
    for d in range(10):
        props.append((5, {n for n in _N if n % 10 == d}))
    for d in range(10):
        props.append((6, {n for n in _N if str(d) in str(n)}))
    return props


_PROPS = _props()


def compute_features(number_set, target):
    ex = [int(x) for x in str(number_set).split(",")]
    t = int(target)
    out = {}
    for f in range(N_FAM):
        shared = [p for fam, p in _PROPS if fam == f and all(e in p for e in ex)]
        out[f"sh_{f}"] = float(len(shared))
        out[f"hit_{f}"] = float(sum(1 for p in shared if t in p))
    out["at_least_min"] = 1.0 if t >= min(ex) else 0.0
    out["at_most_max"] = 1.0 if t <= max(ex) else 0.0
    shared_digit = len({e % 10 for e in ex}) == 1
    out["visible_digit_pattern"] = 1.0 if (len(ex) >= 2 and shared_digit) else 0.0
    # last example's final digit lingers as a candidate only if it is not
    # already a shared (all-example) property
    linger = len(ex) >= 2 and not shared_digit
    out["last_digit_active"] = 1.0 if linger else 0.0
    out["last_digit_match"] = 1.0 if (linger and t % 10 == ex[-1] % 10) else 0.0
    return out


with pm.Model() as model:
    sh = [pm.Data(f"sh_{f}", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64")) for f in range(N_FAM)]
    hit = [pm.Data(f"hit_{f}", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64")) for f in range(N_FAM)]
    ge_min = pm.Data("at_least_min", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    le_max = pm.Data("at_most_max", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    vis = pm.Data("visible_digit_pattern", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    last_on = pm.Data("last_digit_active", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    last_hit = pm.Data("last_digit_match", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))

    intercept = pm.Normal("intercept", mu=-2.0, sigma=1.5)
    slope = pm.HalfNormal("slope", sigma=5.0)
    salience = pm.Dirichlet("salience", a=np.full(N_FAM + 2, 1.5))
    retain = pm.Beta("retain", alpha=2.0, beta=2.0)

        den = den + w * sh[f]
    w_last = recency * salience[FD]
    num = num + w_last * last_hit
    den = den + w_last * last_on
    overlap = num / den
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pm.math.sigmoid(intercept + slope * overlap))

    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm

_N = range(1, 101)
N_FAM = 8
FD = 5


def _props():
    props = []
    props.append((0, {n for n in _N if n % 2 == 1}))
    props.append((0, {n for n in _N if n % 2 == 0}))
    props.append((1, {n for n in _N if n > 1 and all(n % d for d in range(2, int(n ** 0.5) + 1))}))
    props.append((2, {k * k for k in range(1, 11)}))
    props.append((2, {k ** 3 for k in range(1, 5)}))
    for b in range(2, 11):
        props.append((3, {b ** k for k in range(1, 8) if b ** k <= 100}))
    for m in range(3, 13):
        fam = 7 if m in (5, 10) else 4
        props.append((fam, {n for n in _N if n % m == 0}))
    for d in range(10):
        props.append((5, {n for n in _N if n % 10 == d}))
    for d in range(10):
        props.append((6, {n for n in _N if str(d) in str(n)}))
    return props


_PROPS = _props()


def compute_features(number_set, target):
    ex = [int(x) for x in str(number_set).split(",")]
    t = int(target)
    out = {}
    for f in range(N_FAM):
        shared = [p for fam, p in _PROPS if fam == f and all(e in p for e in ex)]
        out[f"sh_{f}"] = float(len(shared))
        out[f"hit_{f}"] = float(sum(1 for p in shared if t in p))
    out["at_least_min"] = 1.0 if t >= min(ex) else 0.0
    out["at_most_max"] = 1.0 if t <= max(ex) else 0.0
    shared_digit = len({e % 10 for e in ex}) == 1
    out["visible_digit_pattern"] = 1.0 if (len(ex) >= 2 and shared_digit) else 0.0
    seed = min(ex)
    is_seed = seed >= 2 and all(e % seed == 0 for e in ex)
    out["seed_shared"] = 1.0 if is_seed else 0.0
    out["seed_hit"] = 1.0 if (is_seed and t % seed == 0) else 0.0
    linger = len(ex) >= 2 and not shared_digit
    out["last_digit_active"] = 1.0 if linger else 0.0
    out["last_digit_match"] = 1.0 if (linger and t % 10 == ex[-1] % 10) else 0.0
    return out


with pm.Model() as model:
    sh = [pm.Data(f"sh_{f}", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64")) for f in range(N_FAM)]
    hit = [pm.Data(f"hit_{f}", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64")) for f in range(N_FAM)]
    ge_min = pm.Data("at_least_min", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    le_max = pm.Data("at_most_max", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    vis = pm.Data("visible_digit_pattern", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    seed_shared = pm.Data("seed_shared", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    seed_hit = pm.Data("seed_hit", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    last_on = pm.Data("last_digit_active", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))
    last_hit = pm.Data("last_digit_match", np.zeros(1, dtype="float64"))

    intercept = pm.Normal("intercept", mu=-2.0, sigma=1.5)
    slope = pm.HalfNormal("slope", sigma=5.0)
    salience = pm.Dirichlet("salience", a=np.full(N_FAM + 3, 1.5))
    retain = pm.Beta("retain", alpha=2.0, beta=2.0)
    recency = pm.HalfNormal("recency", sigma=1.0)

    other_w = 1.0 - (1.0 - retain) * vis
    num = other_w * (salience[N_FAM] * ge_min + salience[N_FAM + 1] * le_max
                     + salience[N_FAM + 2] * seed_hit)
    den = other_w * (salience[N_FAM] + salience[N_FAM + 1] + salience[N_FAM + 2] * seed_shared)
    for f in range(N_FAM):
        w = salience[f] if f == FD else salience[f] * other_w

    w_last = recency * salience[FD]
    num = num + w_last * last_hit
    den = den + w_last * last_on
    overlap = num / den
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pm.math.sigmoid(intercept + slope * overlap))

    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)
EOF
